questions.question: What does Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table list?
questions.explanation: Column 2 lists the proper shipping names and descriptions of hazardous materials.

questions.question: When loading a tank with flammable liquids, what should you do?

options.text: Ground the tank before opening the filling hole.
Ground the tank right before opening the filling hole.
Lock the filling hole while loading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ground the tank before opening the filling hole.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids (unless the engine is needed to run a pump). Ground the tank before opening the filling hole and keep it grounded until after closing the hole.

questions.question: How is a hazardous materials warning shown?

options.text: By wrapping the package in orange.
By separating the item from other cargo and covering it with a sign.

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on vehicles and bulk packages to warn drivers and others about hazardous materials.

questions.question: Who do hazardous materials regulations protect?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials regulations protect you, other people, and the environment.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be placed while you are driving?

options.text: Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or another spot you can reach while your seat belt is fastened. Papers must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Where should you NOT keep hazardous materials shipping papers?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's side door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within your reach while your seat belt is fastened.
On the driver's seat when you are outside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: While driving, keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view and within reach. If you leave the vehicle, place papers on the driver's seat.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed on a truck?

options.text: On the left and right sides.

questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle when required.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are products that pose risks to health, safety, and property during transportation. These include explosives, flammable and poisonous gases, and hazardous solids.

questions.question: How should placards be positioned?

options.text: In any way, as long as they are visible.
So words and numbers read from left to right.
Within three inches of other markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Position placards so words and numbers can be read from left to right. Keep them at least three inches away from other markings.

questions.question: What is the correct way to check tire pressure?

options.text: Push on the tires with your hand.

questions.explanation: You must check each tire at the start of every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only way to check tire pressure correctly.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they suspect a leak in radioactive cargo?

options.text: Go to the local fire department.
Pick up any loose pieces of the material.
Continue driving as long as they don't touch the affected areas.
Do not drive the vehicle until it has been cleaned.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive the vehicle until it has been cleaned.
questions.explanation: If you think there is a leak or broken package in radioactive cargo, tell your dispatcher or supervisor right away. Do not touch or breathe the material. Do not use the vehicle until it has been cleaned or checked with a survey meter.

questions.question: How must a shipper tell a driver about cargo risks?

options.text: By writing a note on plain paper
By putting hazard warning labels on packages
By putting orange dots on packages

questions.correctAnswerText: By putting hazard warning labels on packages
questions.explanation: Shippers must warn drivers about hazardous cargo using shipping papers, hazard warning labels on packages, emergency response information, and placards.

questions.question: When watching a tank being loaded or unloaded, a supervisor must do everything except:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.

questions.explanation: A qualified supervisor must watch the tank loading or unloading. They must be alert, see the tank clearly, stay within 25 feet, know the material hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: How many classes of hazardous materials are there?
questions.explanation: There are nine classes of hazardous materials. Each class shows the risks of that material type.

questions.question: What must be in a vehicle when transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: A driver transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must have an approved gas mask and an emergency kit for fixing leaks in the cargo tank's dome cover plate fittings.

questions.question: What is required of a person supervising tank loading?

options.text: They do not need to be able to move the vehicle.
They must be a licensed firefighter.
They do not need to know about the materials being loaded.
They must stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified supervisor must watch tank loading and unloading. They must be alert, see the tank clearly, stay within 25 feet, know the material hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating for placarded vehicles?
questions.explanation: Placarded vehicles must have a fire extinguisher with an Underwriters Laboratories (UL) rating of at least 10 B:C.

questions.question: What does "RQ" stand for?
questions.explanation: On shipping papers, "RQ" can be used instead of "X" in the "HM" column when a reportable quantity of a material is identified.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be placed?

options.text: Easily visible to anyone entering the cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Easily visible to anyone entering the cab
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers for hazardous materials in a pouch on the driver's side door or where you can reach them while wearing a seat belt. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty cargo tanks for hazardous materials, the driver:

options.text: Can cross railroad tracks without slowing or stopping.
Must slow down at railroad tracks but does not have to stop.
Must stop at railroad crossings before driving across.
Should never drive over railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at railroad crossings before driving across.
questions.explanation: A vehicle with tanks for hazardous materials must always stop at railroad crossings before crossing, even if the tanks are empty.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, you can tell them apart by:

options.text: Non-hazardous materials are written in pencil.
Hazardous materials are written in red ink.
Hazardous materials are written larger than non-hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials must be shown in one of three ways: listed first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" in a column labeled "HM."

questions.question: Your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery. After delivery, turn off the engine ____ you unhook the hoses.
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine when loading or unloading compressed gas, unless your engine runs the pump. If your engine does run the pump, turn it off after the transfer is complete but before unhooking the hoses.

questions.question: If a product needs a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard, you must use it when transporting:

options.text: More than 100 pounds of the product.
More than 50 pounds of the product.
The product in a leaking container.

questions.explanation: For materials that require it, you must always display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard and the correct hazard class placard, no matter how small the amount.

questions.question: Who must provide emergency response information?
questions.explanation: The shipper of hazardous materials must provide emergency response information to drivers.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down while transporting explosives, you may notify other drivers using:

options.text: Standing on the roadway and waving your arms.
Keeping the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, warn other drivers using reflective triangles or electric lights. Do not use warning signals that could cause your cargo to catch fire. Use the same precautions when carrying flammable liquids or gases, even in empty tanks.

questions.question: When you are not in your vehicle, shipping papers for hazardous materials should be:
questions.explanation: Shipping papers for hazardous materials must always be easy to find. When you are not in your vehicle, leave them on the driver's seat.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 items should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: When transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials, cargo heaters are not allowed.

questions.question: Flammable gases are classified as ____ hazards.
questions.explanation: Flammable gases are classified as Class 2 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Who is responsible for identifying the hazard class of materials being shipped?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for identifying the product's ID number, shipping name, hazard class, packing group, and ensuring correct packaging, labels, marking, and placards.
